claim: COLIDE's reference lower-right corner is the upper-left plus the picture's OBJW/OBJH: ADDD OBJW,U (then STD LRX 'LR CORNER OF PLAYER' on the next line). The box the query presents is [UL, UL+size).

COLIDE skips an OFF-SCREEN candidate whose upper-left coord WORD is exactly zero: LDD OBJX,X on the prior line, then BEQ COLLP 'OFF SCREEN' — an object at (0,0) is inactive and passed over even if it would geometrically overlap.

The box overlap test is EXCLUSIVE at the right edge: CMPA LRX (candidate ULX vs reference LRX) followed by BHS COLLP skips when ULX >= LRX, so a candidate exactly touching the right edge does not collide.

Each CANDIDATE computes its own lower-right corner from its OWN picture, dereferenced through OPICT: ADDD [OPICT,X] 'CALC LR' — so a candidate whose upper-left is outside the box still collides when its width/height reach in.

The CENTMP screen-collision address is seeded from the struck object's upper-left coord read as a screen address: LDY OBJX,X 'SCREEN TOP LEFT' — the OBJX/OBJY word doubles as the on-screen beam address (column high byte, row low byte).

One column step in the CENTMP screen address is $100 (256): LEAY $100,Y advances the address by a full column each time the pixel offset overflows a row — i.e. the column lives in the high byte of the coord-as-address word.

The final screen-collision address is stored to CENTMP: STY CENTMP 'SCREEN COLLISION ADDR' — the location an explosion/effect reads to know WHERE on screen the hit was, distinct from the coarse UL/LR box coordinates.
